html:
SMTO-GWT-0080 — SMTO lost contact with the Gateway during a GPU action

GUID: a6b28e9a-3fe2-54ea-89f1-7a04d9ce01ef
Slug: gpu-gateway-lost
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • SMTO didn't get a usable answer from the computer with the GPU. The request may have been refused, or it may already have run there; a stop request may also not have arrived.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and look at the Gateway for the computer with the GPU. Note whether it shows Connection failed. The Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on that computer) must be reachable before SMTO can check or change the GPU.
  2. If it shows Connection failed, make sure that computer is switched on, connected to the network, and its Gateway program is running. SMTO can only reach the GPU through that computer's Gateway.
  3. Once connected, ask SMTO to show the current details for this GPU. Ask for the change again only if it hasn't happened, and never repeat clock or reset requests. The request may have run before the connection dropped, so checking first avoids changing the card twice.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway no longer shows Connection failed, and the GPU details show the setting you wanted.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or that computer. Don't keep resending GPU changes while the Gateway is unreachable; each one might run once it reconnects.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected Gateway did not return a usable GPU operation or cancel result (connection failure or Gateway HTTP error); 400/404/405/422/501 responses mean the request was rejected before dispatch, while other failures may have run.

What this means

  • A GPU operation or cancellation lost usable Gateway communication or received a Gateway HTTP error. Known admission statuses are distinct from failures after possible dispatch. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • A GPU operation or cancellation lost usable Gateway communication or received a Gateway HTTP error. Known admission statuses are distinct from failures after possible dispatch.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect retained HTTP status, failure phase and original execution identity before restoring the route or checking device state.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway's status in Settings > Setup > Gateways and the Gateway log for /gpu/operation or /gpu/cancel. After reconnecting, read gpu.device for the exact UUID and inspect the Gateway job named gpu_ plus the execution ID before any new mutation; a failed /gpu/cancel means the original operation may still be running.
  • Restore the selected route and inspect its retained GPU execution and exact UUID state before another mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • For a mutation, inspect the exact UUID and resolve any active execution or uncertain effect before issuing a new operation. Never replay a reset or an unobservable clock change to infer its result.

How to verify the fix

  • The original operation is reconciled on the same verified Gateway before any repeated configuration.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
